headline_defects_proved.d1_dead_term_is_the_constant_zero: dead_symbols() only emits in-degree-0 symbols, so reverse(s)={} for every s in the predicted-dead set, the 'proven' bucket's guard (reverse(s)!={} AND ...) is FALSE AND _, and proven is empty for EVERY graph and EVERY predictor. Measured: strict_term_proven=[] and strict_term_reverse_nonempty=[] for all three rows. Compounding: the `if |dead| else 1.0` fallback pays a predictor that reports NOTHING dead a perfect 20/20, so the term's range is exactly {0.0, 1.0}. Run 3 called this 'unidentified under a held-out oracle'; it is a constant. eq row 13.
headline_defects_proved.d2_run3_f1_proposal_REFUTED_and_retracte: Run 3 proposed 30*F1 on the grounds that F1 is a lower bound against a partial oracle. False: prec_D<=prec_T holds (|P| fixed) but rec_D<=rec_T does NOT (D={1,2},T={1,2,3,4,5},P={1,2,6} => rec_D=1.0 > rec_T=0.4), and F1 is monotone increasing in r (dF1/dr=2p^2/(p+r)^2>0), so it inherits the sign-indefinite term. Precision is KEPT precisely because it is the only well-posed direction. Retracted numbers retained in the log under harness_score_f1_RETRACTED (64.55/62.40/68.30). eq row 14.

repair: Trace-free certification instead of trace-derived dead accuracy. opaque = bare names of all unresolved call sites; certified = predicted-dead minus every symbol whose bare name matches an opaque name. Zero false positives under the resolver's own soundness, and no execution required. Precondition CHECKED not assumed: a '<complex>' site (call with no extractable callee name, e.g. factory()()) makes the name filter unsound, so the term refuses to score. The precondition FAILS on 3 of 5 real repos (flask, requests, rich). eq rows 15-16.
non_identifiability_result: struct_precision_evaluable is 1.0 for ALL THREE rows while struct_precision spans 0.4286-0.6; the entire difference is unadjudicable edges (2/4/4) -- predicted edges whose caller no fold exercised, which the oracle cannot adjudicate whether real or fabricated. The standing ranking (control 67.55 > mode_b 66.21 > mode_a 62.40) is therefore produced entirely by unadjudicated edges. ranking_identifiable=False is now emitted with a caveat. No aggregator repairs this: precision, F1, min(p,r) and Youden's J are all monotone in the same two contaminated ratios. eq row 17.
reported_against_interest: All three rows certify the SAME single symbol (cache.Cache.stale), so the repair changes what the 20 points MEAN (noise -> sound verdict) and does NOT change which variant wins. The repaired term is 1.0 by construction and is a binary soundness verdict, not a graded signal; the informative certification_rate (0.2/0.3333/0.3333) is reported and deliberately UNSCORED because it rewards shrinking the dead set toward nothing.
prior_art_check: closest art found by me, not hidden: (i) arXiv:2606.09376 Santillana 2026 states verbatim that precision-only metrics reward abstention and resolves it by building a COMPLETE oracle -- unavailable here since T is not enumerable, and it never touches program analysis; (ii) Kalibera & Jones ISSTA 2019 (ACM 3377811.3380441) measures call-graph recall against an incomplete behavioural oracle (median 0.884, 31 Java programs) and names 'invocations initiated by the JVM, without matching call sites' -- structurally the same hole as the <complex> sentinel; (iii) over-approximating unresolved call sites is standard for RECALL (Go VTA, WALA, Closure, Soot) but is never used to gate a DEAD-CODE verdict, and never name-based rather than type/points-to based; (iv) arXiv:2507.00057 (incoherence = provable lower bound without an oracle) shows lower-bound-without-oracle evaluation is active. Not in any of them: the proof that a natural dead-code accuracy-over-prediction-set term is identically zero, the opaque-name certification with its checked precondition, the entry-point-fold unadjudicability condition. novelty 57/100 -> engineering track, no LaTeX paper.
incidental_finding_queued: OUT OF SCOPE for a metric node, queued as N7: dead_symbols() includes imported stdlib symbols (AssertionError, Path, string.hexlify) and load_repo_files flattens tarballs by basename, so the predicted-dead set is polluted on real repos. The old dead_code_acc reads 0.98-1.0 on flask/requests/rich -- it would have looked excellent -- while certification reports the precondition FAILED on 3 of 5. Not fixed here: fixing the pipeline while auditing the instrument destroys the ability to attribute a score change.

headline_retraction: N7's OWN queued premise was half wrong. 'dead_symbols() includes imported stdlib symbols (AssertionError, Path, string.hexlify)' is REFUTED by re-probe: those names appear in ZERO predicted-dead sets across all four real repos, because dead_symbols only iterates locally-defined function/method symbols; rich's pathlib.Path is a call TARGET (a node), never a dead candidate. Retracted in the graph node and in the research md. The BASENAME half of the premise was right and worse than logged (sqlmodel 131/171 files lost, not a handful).
headline_kill: Run 4's certification gate is UNSOUND and its stated 'zero false positives' is withdrawn (eq row 18, node N7b). On synthetic_taint_repo the ungated filter certifies 4 symbols of which 2 are FALSE POSITIVES, by two mechanisms a NAME-based opaque filter cannot see: the string-literal escape (globals()["s"]) and scope (the opaque set is built from the analysis set, which skips tests/, so a test-only reference is invisible). On real repos the demonstrated out-of-scope-reference count is flask 80/111, requests 43/84, rich 120/198 and sqlmodel 107/195 -- and sqlmodel is the ONE real repo where run 4's precondition holds and its gate actually fires, so those 107 are demonstrated, not counterfactual. The global <complex> refusal was not a soundness mechanism; it was the only thing keeping a 55%-false-positive gate switched off, and the single repo where it switched on is where the gate failed. The formula is retained and still measured in src/03_metric_gate.py; only the soundness claim dies.
repair: Replace the global precondition with an occurrence count over the whole reference corpus: certified = {s in dead : occ[leaf(s)] == 1}, counting NAME tokens AND identifier-shaped STRING tokens. Sound because every mechanism that can put a reference to s into the program names s somewhere in the source. Structurally immune to both holes above: there is no opaque-name set to escape and no scope to fall outside of. The <complex> clause disappears entirely, so the term stops refusing on real code -- it now certifies 4/22/22/27 on flask/requests/sqlmodel/rich where run 4 certified 0/0/195/0.
reported_against_interest: The new rule certifies 22 on sqlmodel where run 4's GATED gate certifies 195, so on raw count the replacement looks like a 9x regression. It is not: 107 of those 195 are demonstrated false positives. 22 sound verdicts beats 88 unsound ones. The rule's real cost is its conservatism -- certification_rate is 2-20% on real repos -- and n_blocked_by_string_only is 0-3 everywhere, meaning the blockers are __all__ entries and same-name collisions rather than real callers. That is queued as N9, not claimed as a win.
self_inflicted_bugs_found_this_run: src/04_symbol_domain.py's self_check caught a bug in my OWN fixture on first execution: I had written a symbol as unreferenced while another function called it. The check fired before any number was reported.

run_n7 passed dotted keys (no .py suffix) to the dynamic oracle, which requires .py-suffixed keys; the oracle silently observed ZERO modules and reported a suspiciously round precision of 0.0 on every synthetic fixture. Caught because the number was implausibly round, the same instinct that caught run 3's split_caller_recall bug. Now guarded: no dispatches -> status unvalidated, never a fabricated 0.0.

prior_art_check: Adversarial novelty check returned 25/100; recorded as 28. The mechanism is a direct application of defensive / scope-sensitive soundness (Smaragdakis & Kastrinis, defensive points-to analysis, ECOOP 2018, LIPIcs vol. 109, 23 citations) to a Python CPG: compute sound results where you can, refuse where you cannot. The dead-code-gate use of it (Azad et al., USENIX Security 2019, 132 citations; Role models, CODASPY 2023, 6 citations) and bundler tree-shaking (Rollup/webpack/Terser/esbuild, which assume rather than refuse on unresolvable imports) were all verified as prior art. The exact trace-free occurrence-count rule and the checked-corpus-completeness precondition were NOT found in any source and are recorded as UNVERIFIED-novel rather than novel. Basename flattening as a named bug class in analysis toolchains is UNVERIFIED. The sub-agent's citation verification was itself partial (ACM DL 403s, several items left UNVERIFIED), which is why the score is reported as a range against prior art rather than as a clean number. Novelty 28 -> engineering track, NO LaTeX paper.
